note: Built around the Mataqil musicians of Luxor (the Musicians of the Nile, Metqal Qenawi, Shamandi Metqal) with mizmar and tabl dance pieces for tahtib; the Upper Egypt Ensemble and Aswan Music & Dance Ensemble albums are studio productions for the belly-dance market. Abou Zeïd el Hilali is the Musicians of the Nile's own Hilali epic piece.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. Sa'idi music is mostly played live at weddings and mawlids; what is on record is: four albums by the Musicians of the Nile (Ocora recordings of 1976/79, Real World 1989 and 1996, Long Distance 2006), a large back catalogue of single tracks by Upper Egyptian singers and mizmar bands on Egyptian labels (El Wady Music alone has 15 Metqal Qenawi items on iTunes Egypt, ℗ 1985, and mizmar sa'idi EPs ℗ 1990), studio albums for the belly-dance market (Hollywood Music Center, 2000-2006), and a steady flow of new mizmar sa'idi singles (2023-2026). Real World notes the mizmar village of Djaradjos fell from more than 200 players to about twenty, so the living base is shrinking. An insider's essential list is about 40 recordings, most of them Metqal Qenawi, Shamandi and the Musicians of the Nile.
